name: Greenish sage

sections.title: Greenish sage is a soft, muted green carried into our library from the Japanese traditional color Seiji-iro, named for celadon ware, and it sits 9.6 units from the plain [[sage]].
sections.body:
Our library lists this color under the Japanese name Seiji-iro, written 青磁色, glossed as "celadon color," after the pale green glaze used on Chinese and Japanese celadon stoneware [1]. No book consulted independently dates the name's coinage beyond that gloss, so it is undocumented here [1].

The swatch measures lightness 62, chroma 14 and hue 156 degrees, in the Greens family, low in saturation, which matches the soft, glassy look of a celadon glaze rather than a strong dye [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[surrey-green]], [[morning-blue]], [[sage-green]] and [[bluish-grey-green]], at 4.1, 4.3, 4.4 and 4.7 ΔE [1]. A deeper, more saturated relative in the same name set is [[greenish-bottle-green]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color within range of this swatch appears in 261 of the 23,781 paintings in our archive, about 1.1 percent, as photographed, most often as a highlight [2]. The earliest dated match, a 1470 *Madonna and Child* by an unrecorded painter, predates any celadon-ware link we can verify in a book, so the painting match and the Japanese name are separate strands of evidence, not a shared history, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. Childe Hassam carries it in 3 of 13 dated paintings, 21 times the archive's overall rate [2].

origin.named_after: 青磁 (seiji), celadon ware, + 色 (iro), color
